title: infrastructure-weekly-update-2026-08-03
content:
Weekly infrastructure update (GPU fleet, regions, capacity planning) - 2026-08-03

Owners: Maya Nguyen (infra lead). Collaborators: Liam OConnor, Priya Singh, Diego Ramirez, Chen Wei.

SUMMARY
- Overall fleet health is stable. Average cluster utilization last 7 days: 78% (24h rolling avg). Peak observed yesterday during canary window: 92% for a 20 minute window (08:10-08:30 PDT).
- We are moving forward with a targeted capacity add to relieve peak pressure in us-west1 and europe-west1; plan below.
- No major incidents this week; one latency increase attributed to noisy neighbor causing transient CPU steal on host nodes (details in incidents).

KEY METRICS (last 7 days)
- Token throughput (hosted API): +12% week-over-week driven by a new customer trial and internal load tests.
- GPU tail latency (95th perc): 138ms average, spiked to 210ms during the peak window.
- Instance availability (fleet-level): 99.94%
- Average batch size: 6.1 tokens/request (up from 5.7), batching improvements deployed 2026-07-26 effective.

CAPACITY / PROCUREMENT
- Approved procurement: +24 H100s to be provisioned in us-west1 (GCP) and +8 H100s in europe-west1 (GCP). Expected delivery/provisioning window: 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-13. This is the first tranche of Q3 spot-to-dedicated shift.
- Rationale: sustained peak utilization and forecasted model rollout (new 13B quantized variant for chat workloads) require headroom for stable latency SLOs and canary traffic.
- Cost note: using a mixed reservation strategy (12 reserved + 12 flexible in us-west1) to balance committed cost and burst capacity. Finance reviewed and signed off on the blended unit economics.

REGIONS & ROUTING
- us-west1: highest pressure; targeted add as above. Autoscaler thresholds temporarily tightened for this region to avoid cascading queuing.
- us-east4: utilization moderate; we are keeping a small buffer to failover canaries. No immediate adds planned.
- europe-west1: add of +8 H100s to reduce cross-region failovers for EU customers.
- asia-southeast1: demand remains low; opportunistic spot capacity will continue to be used for batch/off-peak workloads.
- Smart routing update: we rolled out the new policy to prefer local-region dedicated capacity for enterprise tenants (config flags toggled 2026-07-30). Early telemetry looks good (reduced cross-region token travel by ~7%).

INCIDENTS / POST-MORTEMS
- 2026-08-01 07:55 PDT - transient 20-minute latency increase impacting hosted API. Root cause: noisy neighbor process on two GCE host VMs causing CPU steal and host-level interrupts; correlated with background snapshot jobs kicking off on the same hosts.
  - Mitigation applied: migrated affected pods to other hosts, temporarily disabled problematic snapshot job batch.
  - Action items: (1) Diego to add anti-affinity rules for snapshot jobs to avoid colocating with serving nodes (due 2026-08-06). (2) Priya to add host-level monitoring alerts for CPU steal > 5% (due 2026-08-05).

OPERATIONAL CHANGES / RUNBOOKS
- Autoscaler tuning: new conservative scaling profile in us-west1 is now active. Expected effect: fewer scale-up oscillations, slightly higher pre-scale buffer during morning canary windows.
- Scheduler patch v1.9 deployed to 30% of nodes (production canary). This patch improves KV cache recovery after preemption; no regressions observed in canary. Full rollout planned once patch reaches 72h stability.
- Maintenance windows: planned host OS patching in europe-west1 on 2026-08-12 02:00-05:00 UTC (low-impact, will route traffic to us-east4/us-west1 during that window). Notifications sent to CS and select enterprise customers.

CAPACITY PLANNING & FORECAST
- Forecast assumptions: +15-20% monthly increase for hosted API demand due to two incoming mid-market customers scheduled in August. Model changes (quantized 13B) will increase per-request GPU time by ~10% but reduce memory footprint enabling denser packing.
- Short term plan (next 2 weeks): provision hardware above (us-west1 +24 H100s, europe-west1 +8 H100s), complete scheduler patch rollout if stable, and increase reserved capacity for two enterprise tenants as contractual requirement.
- Medium term plan (Q3): evaluate further H100 tranche in us-west1 if utilization remains >80% after provisioning and model rollout stress tests.

MEETING NOTES (Infra standup 2026-08-03)
- Attendees: Maya, Liam, Priya, Diego, Chen, SRE rotation (Arun).
- Decisions: (a) proceed with procurement timeline; (b) postpone decommissioning of legacy P3 instances until 2026-09-01 to avoid capacity cliffs during customer onboarding; (c) prioritize noisy-neighbor mitigations.
- Risks flagged: hardware delivery delays (current ETA contingent on supplier manifest), cost overruns if spot market tightens.

ACTION ITEMS
- Diego Ramirez: implement anti-affinity for snapshot jobs and add integration test to CI for job placement (due 2026-08-06).
- Priya Singh: create host-level CPU steal alert + dashboard and runbook (due 2026-08-05).
- Chen Wei: monitor scheduler v1.9 canary and report any KV cache regressions (ongoing, next report 2026-08-07).
- Liam OConnor: coordinate hardware provisioning with cloud provider and vendor (confirm rack availability and expected provisioning dates) (due 2026-08-06).
- Maya Nguyen: finalize reservation purchase order and notify finance (done 2026-08-03).

BLOCKERS / NEEDS FROM OTHER TEAMS
- Procurement: confirmation of delivery ETA from vendor for H100 tranche (blocked until vendor reply; Liam is chasing).
- Legal/Finance: finalize updated reserved instance agreement for europe-west1 (Finance reviewed; Legal needs to sign off by 2026-08-07).
- CS/GTM: heads-up to enterprise customers for the maintenance window (PR requested to notify enterprise via email on 2026-08-05).

NOTES / CONTEXT
- Quantization improvements from applied-ml team continue to free up memory allowing denser packing of model KV caches; this contributed to a ~6% capacity headroom improvement last week. Appreciate the applied-ml/serving-runtime collaboration on this.
- We should expect a temporary increase in rolling restarts as we finish scheduler patch rollout; plan is to coordinate with SRE for off-peak windows and use canary throttles.

LOOKAHEAD (next update)
- Confirm H100 delivery dates and put provisioning tickets in place.
- Report on scheduler v1.9 full rollout progress and any observed regressions.
- Publish updated capacity forecast post-provisioning and post-model-rollout stress tests.

If you have questions or want a deeper breakdown (per-customer impact, per-queue latency histograms), ping me or drop requests in #infra-weekly.

-- Maya
